findings.title: [P2] Redact provider errors before recording or printing them
findings.body: Anthropic error messages flow from the HTTP response into ProviderContextLimitError and then directly into `message_redacted` through `str(_exc)`. The same raw exception is printed in stderr JSON below. If a provider or proxy error echoes a credential, it is exposed in operator logs regardless of downstream audit redaction. The supplied `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` contains a concrete credential-shaped example. Apply the existing redaction helper before either sink.
findings.description: Anthropic error messages flow from the HTTP response into ProviderContextLimitError and then directly into `message_redacted` through `str(_exc)`. The same raw exception is printed in stderr JSON below. If a provider or proxy error echoes a credential, it is exposed in operator logs regardless of downstream audit redaction. The supplied `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` contains a concrete credential-shaped example. Apply the existing redaction helper before either sink.
findings.failure_mode: Anthropic error messages flow from the HTTP response into ProviderContextLimitError and then directly into `message_redacted` through `str(_exc)`.

findings.cross_file_justification: anthropic_adapter.py (diff-touched) builds ProviderContextLimitError from regex-parsed provider error text via parse_context_limit(); cheval.py (diff-touched) persists those numbers through routing/ceiling.record_observed (omitted from the diff) and reads them back on every later call via observed_for().
findings.description: The new self-correction loop turns numbers scraped out of an HTTP 400/413 error body into a persistent bound. `_calibration_needed_exit` accepts any positive `observed` and passes `provider_limit` through with no sanity check (no floor, no relation to `_walk_estimate`, no relation to the catalog's `probed_ceiling`/`context_window`). Per the e2e tests the stored bound becomes `limit + 1`, so a single response of the shape `prompt is too long: 5 tokens > 4 maximum` from the configured `endpoint` (an enterprise gateway, a misbehaving proxy returning 413 with a matching body, or anything that can speak to the operator's endpoint URL) records a bound of 4 and every subsequent invocation of that (provider, model) is preempted with CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE before dispatch until an operator runs the probe tool. When the message carries no numbers, `_obs` falls back to `_walk_estimate` (or 0 when unset), so a proxy-level 413 on a small request lowers the bound to that request's size. The store file is read with `_observed_for()` on every hop in `_lookup_max_input_tokens`, so poisoning it (via response text, or directly if the `.run/ceiling-observed.json` path lacks the symlink/regular-file guards `resolve_cost_ledger_path` applies to the cost ledger) is a durable denial of the model entry. ceiling.py was not in the reviewed diff, so the store's own write/read hardening could not be verified.
findings.failure_mode: One malformed or hostile context-limit response permanently (until manual calibration) forces preempt for a model entry; a writable or symlinked observed-store path has the same effect without any provider involvement.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate before recording: require `provider_limit >= FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS` and `observed_input_tokens` within a plausible band of `_walk_estimate` (e.g. 0.5x..2x) and never above `context_window`; refuse to lower the bound below the catalog `probed_ceiling` from a single observation (require N consistent observations or only lower when the request itself was above the probed bound); treat a 413 with no parseable numbers as non-recordable. In ceiling.py, open the store with O_NOFOLLOW, reject non-regular files, and canonicalize the env-supplied path the way `resolve_cost_ledger_path` does.

findings.cross_file_justification: The message originates as the raw provider error body `_msg` in anthropic_adapter.py (both streaming and non-streaming paths) and is written into the MODELINV envelope and stderr JSON by cheval.py; whether it is redacted depends on audit/modelinv.redact_payload_strings and _error_json, neither of which is in the diff.
findings.description: `_calibration_needed_exit` copies the provider's error text verbatim into `models_failed[].message_redacted` and into the stderr `_error_json` payload (`f"{_exc} — not walked..."`). No redaction is applied at the write site despite the field name; the diff relies on emit-time scrubbing elsewhere. The shipped test `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` patches `redact_payload_strings` to identity and still asserts the key is absent, which means either redaction happens in a layer not shown or the test does not pass against this code. The `_calib` dict also embeds `_observed_store_path()` (an absolute filesystem path) into the envelope and operator log.
findings.failure_mode: A provider or gateway error body that echoes request fragments or credentials lands unredacted in the audit chain and operator stderr; absolute local paths leak into envelopes that may be shipped off-host.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the message through the redaction helper at the write site (both `message_redacted` and the `_error_json` text), cap its length, and record the store path relative to the project root or omit it from the envelope.

findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the head entry's pre-flight outcome but consulted inside the per-hop loop for every fallback hop (RateLimitError at 2297, ProviderContextLimitError at 2256). The RateLimitError short-circuit also does not check whether the 429 was token-limited. Consequence: after the head fails for a walkable reason, any 429 on a calibrated fallback ends the invocation as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED and appends a calibration row against the fallback model, and a provider verdict on that fallback is misclassified as CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT. The accompanying e2e tests (`test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head`, `test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop`) specify the opposite behaviour, so the diffed code and the tests disagree.
findings.failure_mode: Availability: a chain that should walk to a verified fallback instead exits on an ordinary rate limit, and the observed store accumulates rows for models that were never above their bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Track unverified status per hop (set it from a per-hop gate decision, reset it on each iteration) and gate the 429 short-circuit on `getattr(_e, 'token_limited', False)`.

findings.description: When the provider's context-limit error arrives on the final permitted attempt, the shrink branch sets the new `max_tokens` and `continue`s, the loop ends, and the function falls through to its retries-exhausted path without `last_typed_error` having been set for this class. cheval's `except ProviderContextLimitError` is bypassed, so the non-walk rule and the observed-bound record do not run and the same oversized payload is sent to the next hop.
findings.failure_mode: The D-1.1b guarantee (provider verdict is never walked) silently does not hold when max_retries is exhausted on the shrink attempt.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `last_typed_error = e` before `continue`, and only shrink-and-retry when another attempt is actually available; otherwise `raise` immediately.

findings.description: `_mult` accepts any positive float, including `inf` (YAML `.inf` or `1e400`) and values below 1.0. `calculate_total_cost` then does `int(inp_cost * im)`, which raises OverflowError for infinity after the provider call has already been billed, losing the ledger row and the daily-spend update. A multiplier under 1.0 silently under-bills long-context requests in the ledger.
findings.failure_mode: Catalog typo turns into a post-call crash that drops the cost record, or into systematic under-counting of the premium tier.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `math.isfinite(m)` and `m >= 1.0`; reject the block (log and fall back to no premium) otherwise.

findings.description: The new GET transport hands the catalog `endpoint` straight to `urllib.request.urlopen` with the provider's `x-api-key` attached and reads the whole body unbounded. There is no scheme check (urllib honours `file://` and `ftp://`) and no response-size cap. The URL is operator-config-controlled so this is hardening rather than a direct exploit, but `health_check` is called from status tooling and now sends the key to whatever `endpoint` resolves to without the request-body shape that `http_post` imposes.
findings.failure_mode: A mis-set or hostile endpoint receives the API key on a GET, or a slow/huge response stalls the health probe beyond its intended 15 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the endpoint scheme is https (http only for explicit localhost), cap `resp.read()` to a few KB for the probe, and share the scheme check with `http_post`.
